title: Asset Allocation in a new regime for bond yields
gist: Ahead of a multi-asset strategy webinar led by Javier Corominas, the promotional text previews the strategist's live positioning: overweight global equities (especially the US) on broadening EPS momentum, a live debate on rotating Japan into Europe, and open questions on whether 5% US 10y yields are durable and whether EM local bonds now beat traditional bonds as portfolio ballast.

insights.claim: Heading into year-end 2026, record EPS momentum broadening across Europe and emerging markets is cited as the basis for staying overweight global equities, with a further overweight to US equities within that allocation.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: A broadening (not just US-led) EPS momentum picture is the stated trigger for staying long risk assets going into year end; investors can watch European and EM earnings revisions as a confirming or disconfirming signal.
insights.quote: Going into year end, with record EPS momentum broadening across Europe and EM, we stay overweight global equities — and within that, overweight the US.
insights.locator: Going into year end, with record EPS momentum

insights.claim: Financial conditions are judged not yet restrictive because the hurdle rate needed to slow AI-related capital expenditure sits well above prevailing interest rates, implying current rate levels are unlikely to choke off AI capex growth.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: If the rate level needed to actually deter AI capital spending is well above today's rates, the AI infrastructure investment cycle — and equities levered to it — can keep running even as rates stay elevated, reducing near-term downside risk from a higher-for-longer rate backdrop.
insights.quote: Financial conditions are not yet restrictive, and the hurdle rate needed to arrest AI capex sits well above prevailing interest rates.
insights.locator: Financial conditions are not yet restrictive

insights.claim: Whether to rotate out of expensive Japanese equities into European equities, where earnings momentum is improving, is being actively weighed as a potential portfolio shift beyond the core US overweight.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Investors overweight Japan on valuation-agnostic momentum should watch for confirmation of improving European earnings as a signal to rotate exposure toward Europe instead.
insights.quote: we ask whether it is time to rotate out of expensive Japanese equities into Europe, where earnings momentum is improving

themes.theme: New bond-yield regime and portfolio ballast

insights.claim: Whether US 10-year Treasury yields at 5% are durable, rather than a transient spike, is posed as an open and central question for the current bond-yield regime.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: If 5% proves to be a durable floor rather than a peak, duration exposure, equity valuation multiples, and cross-asset hedging strategies all need repricing around a structurally higher long-end yield.

insights.claim: In an environment of positive stock-bond correlations and waning structural demand for developed-market government bonds, emerging-market local-currency bonds are floated as potentially better portfolio ballast than traditional government bonds.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: This challenges the standard 60/40 assumption that government bonds reliably hedge equity risk; if stock-bond correlations stay positive, investors may need to shift diversifying fixed-income allocations toward EM local debt instead of DM duration.
insights.quote: In a world of positive stock-bond correlations and waning structural demand, are EM local bonds the better portfolio ballast?

insights.claim: The multi-asset strategy service led by Javier Corominas combines tactical calls over a 6-12 month horizon with strategic asset allocation over 5-plus years, both derived from macro-driven frameworks and proprietary quantitative models applied across global assets and sectors.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: The dual tactical/strategic, macro-plus-quant framework is the lens through which the service's specific calls (equity overweight, Japan-to-Europe rotation, EM bonds as ballast) should be read and weighted.
insights.quote: the service covers both tactical (6–12m) and strategic (5y+) asset allocation across global assets and sectors, driven by actionable, macro-inspired frameworks and proprietary quantitative models
insights.locator: Led by Javier Corominas, Chief Multi-Asset Strategist
